This game has developed in such a weird way, and I haven't kept up with it because everytime I try to play this game I'm compelled to log off and play something else. 

Playing the mini-games isn't fun, not only are they all repetitive, most of the time the assists & magnetisation make it impossible or really annoying to complete. They have fixed some of these missions issues, but the problem presists in the open world with rails and ledges. It's hard to get a flow in this game when the world is just not that skateable.
Another gripe I have is the bowls, quarter pipes, and vert ramps being so small. It's hard to skate on a lot of these structures, most of it doesn't even go well together. Why give me a pool to skate in and make the walls super shallow so I gain no speed? 
There's a lot of different areas to explore and skate especially with climbing & whatnot, but moving around the map on the board and trying to just have fun along the way is so difficult. 

I don't think I'll be playing this game anytime soon again, not until I see genuine improvement in content given to the player rather than a price-tag to open up features that were included when you bought the game "but we're moving to a free-to-play model". claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game requires an EA account and is always online.

citations.review_text:
I played quite a good amount once it first released publicly (firstly via EA's app, then I moved to Steam) but burned myself out.
It worked quite well on my system at the time; good FPS and minimal crashes.

I tried to get back into it around May / June 2026 and had issues with kernel-level anti cheat errors which I couldn't figure out how to resolve, so couldn't even launch the game.

Tried it again today (Aug 2026) and didn't even see a splash screen, it made my PC fully reboot with 0 warning.

I am going to uninstall it now, which is a shame but it's a bit too broken to trust.

I may try again in a year or two and update this review if I do have better results.

Skate. feels like a soulless, oversaturated, microtransaction filled version of what made the original series special.

Typical EA features:

- Free to play
- Online only
- Requires a EA account to play
- Cosmetic pop ups everywhere
- Slow pointless levelling system designed to keep players ''entertained''

Meanwhile Skate 3 a game over 15 years old! is still better in almost every aspect. gameplay, progression, atmosphere, creativity, soundtracks, charm, and overall design. It actually felt like a skateboarding game made by people who understood skate culture instead of a live service product.

Modern gaming somehow reached a point where booting up an emulator to play Skate 3 is more fun than playing a brand new entry in the series.

That says everything.

I really didn't mind the f2p it was the always online with stutter when over crowded which leads to smaller ollies and tricks, more bails and failing challenges. On top of that the game has been busted for a WHILE with UI bugs that makes it unplayable. It'd be nice if they fixed a major issue that seems to plague AMD gpus.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience technical problems upon launching the game, including infinite loading screens, black screens, and hard crashes.

citations.review_text:
I played quite a good amount once it first released publicly (firstly via EA's app, then I moved to Steam) but burned myself out.
It worked quite well on my system at the time; good FPS and minimal crashes.

I tried to get back into it around May / June 2026 and had issues with kernel-level anti cheat errors which I couldn't figure out how to resolve, so couldn't even launch the game.

Tried it again today (Aug 2026) and didn't even see a splash screen, it made my PC fully reboot with 0 warning.

I am going to uninstall it now, which is a shame but it's a bit too broken to trust.

I may try again in a year or two and update this review if I do have better results.

I'm new to skate franchise and from a fresh perspective; i enjoy the controls to a point, but sometimes the game doesn't register the move i've done as being correct even though my input was correct, so some challenges become bricked. When it works, it feels great. Unfortunately there are glaring issues that are heavily affecting my review.
The infinite loading screens and black screens requiring an alt-f4 to solve: 
(Disclaimer, don't mess with your bios unless you know what you're doing) Following a not too far away bios/gpu update, there was an overclocking/compatibility issue that i noticed since a couple other heavy games were having crash to desktop issues including this game. Upon defaulting the overclock then re-engaging it (DOCP1), things were running fine (beside the occasional blackscreen/loading-screen-lock which i know is an optimization issue with this game because the other heavy games stopped having CTD issues after disabling and re-enabling the PCs overclock). It could also be the GPU 50 series or bios having stability issues after certain updates, but what's frustrating is how long these issues continue on after further updates. I'm not sure what limitations would exist for an incredibly wealthy company such as EA, but their track record isn't great so i'm not expecting any improvement. So the performance and aggressive microtransactions are the major deterrent for me continuing to enjoy this game.

Edit: To fix the black screen startup error: Start the game but quickly click into your browser. Wait for the game to load before swapping over from the browser to the game. Ridiculous this hasn't been addressed by EA yet. I still get occasional crashes though and won't change to recommend until these technical issues are fixed.

I played the game for roughly 20 minutes and the game ran fine and was fun. However, the second and all subsequent starts of the game load to an immediate black screen and hard crash my computer. It disables all inputs so alt-tab, ctrl-alt-delete, etc. don't work. Nothing on my controller allows me to regain access to the computer either and I have to do a hard reset.

I have verified the files and it tells me they successfully check out. I then uninstalled and reinstalled the entire game to no avail. For reference, I have played hundred of games and never had this issue. Not sure how the game made it past QA testing.

CONS : No pro skaters in game (apparently zekyzek is "pro" enough to have his own challenges and event), no real customization for your character, too many bugs, too many challenges that dont make sense, "community made parks" dont look/feel finished, god awful events, no hall of meat, no death race, no s.k.a.t.e., boring cosmetics, "good" cosmetics behind battlepass, no offline play, annoying voices talking to you every 24/7 cause you landed a clean ollie, obstacles that lead you to nowhere, game is to focused on parkour and not enough attention into the main focus of the game SKATE, music that plays feels like going into a target or an H&M... etc. etc.

i can go on for hours how disappointed i am with this game. i want to enjoy it so badly but whenever i get back on i get bored within 30mins of gameplay. there is nothing to do on this game. i fear this game will shut down within the next year or 2. typical EA killing games just to get a profit out of the players.

[h1]yikes.[/h1]
[b]this game is what you get when you lobotomize skate culture of everything that makes it unique/distinct and inject the lifeless corpse with bland AI slop until the nipples go stiff.[/b]

I know it isn't groundbreaking to say 'everything EA touches turns to ♥♥♥♥'.  But ladies & gentlemen, this is something special.  100% pure, lab-grade, crystalline-cringe; straight off the monocrystal.  You just can't GET this stuff anywhere else, folks!

[list]
[b]PROS[/b]
[*] mechanically, its similar enough to the OG skate games that there is still *some* fun to be had (before you burn through the limited content and it starts recycling itself)
[*] trick animations look decent
[*] [b] you can mute the voice overs [/b]
[/list]

[list]
[b]CONS[/b]
[*] no representation of actual skaters or skate culture
[*] aesthetic best described as 'AI-fortnite-slop' meets 'groomer-Zumiez-manager'
[*] you thought we were getting Skate 4? [b]"sir, this is a V-buck vending machine"[/b]
[*] terribly designed spots throughout the city; how is a city 'built by skaters' [i]this[/i] bad for skating?
[*] the 'missions' are just endless condescending tutorials?
[*] no hall of meat
[*] everything is very clearly written by AI
[*] paywalled location access
[*] the audacity to put microtransactions in an UNFINISHED GAME
[*] insanely intrusive kernel-level anti-cheat, but for why?
[*] rampant bugs/glitches, constant hangups/crashes
[/list]

I could EASILY go on, but you get the idea.  [b] If this game was my introduction to skateboarding, I never would have touched a board.[/b] They tried to make it accessible to anyone, and made it unwanted by literally everyone.  I genuinely didn't know it was possible to portray skateboarding THIS lame, so I guess congrats on lowering the bar?

[h1] FYI 95% of the articles/reviews glazing this game online were written by AI (probably EA putting those tokens to use themselves).  YUCK.  I'd ask for my money back but it's 2026 and I'm not gullible enough t…

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the presence of multiple in-game currencies and a battle pass system that requires extra purchases to complete or access map areas.

citations.review_text: Unnecessary anti-cheat makes this otherwise fine game impossible to play on Steam Deck/Linux. Keyword *fine*, not good. As of writing, this game has FOUR in-game currencies and a battle-pass, none of which improve the game-play.

I purchased this for the early access and out of good faith that the devs were going to keep up the spirit of the previous Skate games. I was incredibly wrong and when they released a battlepass for a skateboarding game I knew it was only downhill from there. I tried to give them the benefit of the doubt but when it finally released you couldn't fully complete the battlepass by playing the game/completing events/challenges you had to buy their in-game tickets/currency to buy your way through the rest of it. I never bothered to stick around long enough to find out if they backtracked that and decided to make it something you could complete without paying extra for it.

For a free to play game it offers a good free roaming experience. There are no tricks behind a paywall. There is a battlepass system that offers costmetics and earlier access to certain skate areas.  Those areas can be unlocked for 24 hours with ingame currency. There's a replay system that's solid for recording tricks and you can place obstacles on the ground to skate on. There are assignments you can do on the map to earn ingame currency, once is a challenge, twice is a repetition and trice is a drag. Once the novelty of these assigments runs out the game falls flat but that does not come once you've already invested many hours into this free-to-play game.
The only good map costs in-game currency to visit for 24 hours at a time LOL

EA is very out of touch. 
Edit 6-22-26: I realized after writing this review, after a long work day I come home and find myself playing this corpo slop version of a game I put countless hours into. However, less enjoyable than the previous title, by all accounts, I accepted that I will probably be playing this mess of a game until there is another entry in the series. 

At its core, Skate is a fun sandbox experience that is lacking in a lot of areas. the micro transaction side of things is pretty gross, but its an EA game so thats just part of the "experience". This Go Skate event was actually pretty solid, the rewards for participating in it were actually pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and very forgettable. The basic unlocks of the game are also pretty bad, and there really hasn't been much added in terms of unlocking through non monetized means. The mission system, and the missions themselves are also just not fun, and are bugged the majority of the time. 

Also a big problem for me is the "Tix" system, its currency for the battle pass that you earn in game, but can also purchase with real money. My problem is Tix have a lifespan, so right now i have 24000 tix, and theres nothing that really catches my eye in the battlepass. i have been playing the entire past week grinding, obtaining tix, for the next battlepass whenever it drops, to hopefully get something neat with my hard earned currency. Nope, not how it works, tix expire at the end of the season, but not only do they expire, they auto purchase all of the actual ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ items in the battlepass that i purposefully am avoiding. i dont want your ugly sports themed garbage. i dont want your absolutely atrocious "Golden Shoes" (seriously who greenlit that ♥♥♥♥)? why cant devs look at the helldivers battlepass system as inspiration? i dont even play that game anymore but when i loaded it up the other day i had access to every pass they've released since it came out. if skate allowed us to use "san van bucks" to buy passes that hav…

ZERO innovation here folks!!! Just a bunch of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ ideas mashed together in order to sell you fake skateboarding culture via microtransactions.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe missing features from past entries such as a single-player story campaign and professional skaters.

citations.review_text:
Don't bother if you're a fan of the series; this game is nothing but F2P microtransaction trash.

In another Halo: Infinite type debacle this game claimed F2P and Early Access as excuses for delivering an undercooked product that somehow has a fully functioning store before being "content complete". The braindead leaders at Full Circle and EA decided, in their infinite lack of wisdom, that it would be smart to release a Skate game with no single player story, no pro skaters, no handplants, no fingerflps, no darkslides, no meaningful competitive modes, ♥♥♥♥♥♥ janky footplants, a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ janky replay editor, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ servers and performance optimization. 

The game has been out for nearly a year and you still can't play SKATE in a skate game, there's still no story or pro skaters, and the store is still operating on a FOMO model. The physics and co-op WERE fun, but each progressively less inspired update also seems to break the game even more. 

Basically save yourself some time and skip this low effort slopfest.

If u like realistic skating u can have a great time on this game, especially if u played skaterXL with mods, but if u are a fan of the skate series this will let u down, no story, repetitive missions and overall a pretty bad game.
